script.base: Spread and total are not in the pack, so the script is inferred only from two-game form. KC has the clearer offense: Kenneth Walker 47 carries for 290 yards plus 16 targets for 79 receiving yards, Travis Kelce 16 targets for 172 yards, and Mahomes 0.36 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=24) against 0.10 when not blitzed. MIA blitzes 41% and its QB is -0.50 EPA vs blitz (n=18) vs +0.12 with no blitz, while KC has allowed only 2 passes of 20+ on 63 attempts. Base case: KC controls a competitive game, stays balanced, Walker keeps the carry share, and Kelce is the first answer to the blitz in the middle.
script.flip1: MIA hangs around or leads and KC passes more. Walker carries slide toward the Emmett Johnson/Mahomes share (10 and 6 carries over two games) but his 8 targets per game can still feed rush+rec; Kelce, Rashee Rice (8 targets, 102 yards) and Xavier Worthy (13 targets) see more volume.
script.flip2: KC jumps ahead early and clocks it. Walker rushing stays live or rises, and Kelce/Worthy/Tyquan Thornton receiving stalls the way a big lead stalls skill-player yards. That flip helps a Walker rush leg and is the main way a Kelce over loses.

matchup.pressure: MIA blitz rate 41%. Mahomes is better into that look (0.36 EPA, n=24) than when not blitzed (0.10), so pressure should feed quick answers to Kelce and check-downs to Walker/Johnson rather than kill KC deep yards. KC blitzes 32%. MIA's QB falls apart vs blitz (-0.50 EPA, n=18) vs +0.12 with no blitz, which caps Miami explosives; passing yards are not a legal market here.
matchup.bleeds: MIA run defense allows 3.95 YPC and 6 runs of 10+ in two games — average, not a wall and not a soft box. MIA's pass bleed is the middle (11.27 YPA) plus explosives (6 of 20+ on 52 attempts). KC allows 3.93 YPC and 5 runs of 10+, but only 2 passes of 20+ on 63 attempts, with the right side at 4.04 YPA.
matchup.overlap: Kelce is the yards leader (172 rec, 85 air on 16 targets) into the exact area MIA bleeds (middle 11.27 YPA) and into a 41% blitz Mahomes has crushed. Walker is the usage overlap: about 23.5 carries and 8 targets a game against a run defense that has already leaked 6 runs of 10+ and a blitz that can spill check-downs to the back.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Walker is the KC skill engine — 47 carries for 290 and 16 targets for 79 over two games, about 184 rush+rec per game — and 109.5 sits roughly 70 yards under that role against a MIA run defense at 3.95 YPC that has allowed 6 runs of 10+.
edge_players.must_be_true: He is active for a full complement (no snap limit in the pack), keeps the 47-to-10 carry edge over Emmett Johnson, and KC gets a normal play count whether they lead or trail.
edge_players.kills_it: A low-play slog or a committee cut to about 12 carries and 2-3 targets, or a late inactive. 18 carries at a regressed 4.0 YPC (72) plus 20 receiving is 92 and loses to 109.5.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Kelce is the primary target at 16 targets and 172 yards (86 per game) and he works the middle, where MIA allows 11.27 YPA, into a 41% blitz Mahomes has played at 0.36 EPA.
edge_players.must_be_true: He plays a full route share, stays the first read vs pressure, and KC does not spend the second half only running clock.
edge_players.kills_it: Flip-2 lead that clocks Kelce down to 3-4 targets, or an uncharted bracket (no shell data in the pack) that pushes explosives to Worthy and Thornton. Four targets at 10 yards is 40 and loses to 52.5.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost because the two-game peaks were the trap and the missing spread hid a bad script. Miami loaded the box after Walker's 290-yard fortnight, Johnson took the change-of-pace, and a short second half left Walker around 14 carries for 55 plus a couple of catches, under 109.5 combined. Kelce was bracketed — shell charting was never in the pack — and a KC lead let them run, so he finished near 4 for 38 while the two explosives MIA still allows (6 of 20+ on 52 throws) went to Worthy and Thornton. That counter-case is real on sample size and the clock-kill flip, which is why Kelce is only a lean; it is not stronger than Walker's carry-and-target gap, so the Walker leg stays.
slip_story: One story only: KC's offense functions against a 41% blitz and a middle that leaks. Walker rush+rec over and Kelce rec-yards over win together in a competitive KC-control game. Do not add a pure clock-kill stack or a game under (total not in the pack). rushrec, not rush alone, is what keeps Walker alive if flip1 makes the game pass-heavy. MIA unders (Achane rush under 60.5, Washington under 40.5) are a different story and were not used.
